counterevidence_considered.description: The only candidate concern found: all 26 compartments come from a single contiguous burned block, so one could ask whether compartments are truly independent of each other. This is a spatial-autocorrelation question, not repeated entry of the same authorized independent unit, and the description itself declares the compartments physically separated and treats them as 13 independent values per group, so it does not demonstrate the issue class under review.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: single contiguous burn area subdivided into 26 physically separated compartments

source_refs.quoted_text:
A wildfire burned a contiguous block of montane pine forest on Kelsang Ridge.
For post-fire management the burned block was split into 26 compartments of
roughly equal size, separated from one another by ridgelines and drainages.

The seeding treatment was applied to whole compartments, and the outcome is
measured at the same whole-compartment scale, so a comparison between the two
treatment groups has 13 independent values on each side.

evidence.description: The data description defines the independent unit as the compartment and states each compartment appears exactly once, giving 26 data rows for 26 compartments.
evidence.observed_value: 26 compartments, 26 rows, one row per compartment

evidence.description: The input CSV contains exactly 26 data rows with compartment_id values BC-01 through BC-26, each value appearing exactly once; no independent unit contributes more than one row to the t-test.

evidence.description: The workflow actively enforces one row per independent unit before running the row-independent procedure: count_units raises an error if any compartment_id appears more than once, and this check runs before the Welch t-test on the row-level values.
evidence.observed_value: duplicate-unit guard raises ValueError; test operates on 13 vs 13 compartment-level values

evidence.description: The report's stated design and independence check match the data: treatment was assigned and the outcome measured at the same whole-compartment scale, rows read equals distinct compartments (26), and no sub-unit or repeat-visit rows enter the test.
evidence.observed_value: Rows read: 26; Distinct compartments: 26; rows per compartment: 1

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to demonstrate the issue by checking every route through which one independent unit could contribute multiple rows to the row-independent Welch t-test: (1) I scanned all 26 data rows in data/input.csv for duplicate compartment_id values (BC-01 through BC-26 each appear exactly once, 13 per treatment arm); (2) I checked whether the workflow expands rows into sub-unit records or reuses any row in both group vectors (the seeded/natural filters on aerial_seeding are mutually exclusive and exhaustive, and each row enters exactly one vector once); (3) I checked whether the test inputs are anything other than one value per compartment (stats.ttest_ind receives 13 and 13 compartment-level values); (4) I checked the report's claimed counts against the code and data (26 rows, 26 distinct units, df = 23.5 consistent with n = 13 vs 13 Welch). Every route came up empty, and the workflow additionally has a guard that would have aborted the analysis on any duplicated compartment_id, so the issue class could not be demonstrated.
